text:
Maya: Quick handoff — I'm wrapping the day shift. TL;DR: canary rollout at 10%, two PRs need review, warm-cache job at 23:45 might cause a short GPU memory spike.

Maya: Canary details: model-service v1.2.3 -> slot-b (us-west-2). Traffic at 10%. Watch /v1/generate p95 and request_errors. Canary link: https://deploys.redwood/canary/slot-b (internal).

Sam: Got it — I'll watch latency and set a 5m dashboard alert for p95 > 350ms.

Maya: Two PRs to unblock ramp: #4523 batching refactor (risk: changes how small requests are batched, could increase tail latency), #4531 kv-cache TTL tweak (risk: transient cold-starts after TTL shorten). Both have CI green but need one more review.

Sam: I can take #4523 now, aiming to review in 30m. @Priya can you eyeball #4531? Specifically look at the TTL change in caching layer.

Priya: On it. I'll run the local repro and check kv hit/miss distribution. If I see >5% miss after TTL change I'll block.

Luca: I'm on deck from 23:30 PT -> 04:00 PT for overnight. If the canary needs to be rolled back, prefer manual rollback to keep visibility.

Maya: Warm-cache job scheduled at 23:45 (job: warm-cache-prod). It prefetches common prefixes; expected ~90s runtime and a short GPU mem spike on node pool pool-inference-2. If you see OOMs or node evictions, scale down canary or pause the warm job.

Priya: Note on alerts — add temporary suppressor for noise on cache_miss_rate alert between 23:40-23:55 if the job runs. Otherwise: action if cache_miss_rate > 5% for 2 consecutive minutes.

Sam: Quick check command for canary pods/status:
```bash
kubectl --context=prod get pods -n inference -l release=slot-b -o wide
kubectl --context=prod logs -n inference -l release=slot-b -c model-container --tail=100
```

Sam: I'll also tail the latency dashboard and post a screenshot if p95 goes > 350ms for more than 3mins.

Oncall Bot: [deploy] canary rollout 1.2.3 -> slot-b started by @Maya at 2026-03-18T20:12:01Z.

Maya: Action items: Sam - review #4523 and monitor p95; Priya - validate TTL change and warm-cache behaviour; Luca - be ready to rollback and coordinate with infra if nodes evict. I'll keep monitoring and will DM if I see churn.

Luca: ack. I'll keep Slack audible.

Priya: Found a small edge in #4531 (TTL config fallback missing). Pushing a tiny fix now, will request review afterward.

Sam: Reviewed #4523 — left one comment about batching window default (changed from 10ms -> 25ms). If we keep 25ms we should test under tail load; otherwise revert to 10ms.

Maya: Good catch. Let's not change defaults in the canary. Priya, if your TTL fix is minor, we can include it in the canary patch; otherwise keep separate and watch.

Priya: Merge PR with TTL fallback fix, will ping when done.

Oncall Bot: [job] warm-cache-prod started at 2026-03-18T23:45:00Z (expected ~90s).

Sam: Seeing a small p95 blip to ~380ms for two intervals coinciding with warm-cache job. p95 back to 310ms now. No errors. Posting metrics snapshot. :thumbsup:

Maya: Thanks — sounds healthy. If anything trends up for >5mins escalate.

Luca: If we need to roll back: runbook link -> https://runbooks.redwood/canary-rollback. Primary rollback command: `kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/model-service --to-revision=<prev>` (double-check revision).

Maya: Leaving notes in the handoff doc: canary -> 10% steady, warm-cache ran and caused transient p95 blip but recovered, PR #4531 merged with TTL fallback, #4523 needs follow-up on batching window.

Sam: Closing loop — I'll keep monitoring for the next hour and will escalate if p95 > 350ms for 3 consecutive mins.

Priya: All green from my side after the fix, no increased miss rates.

Maya: Thanks team. Handing off to Luca; ping me if anything suspicious.

Luca: Took over. Notes captured. Good luck and see you in the morning.

Maya: :wave:
